proof_summary: Successive binomial coefficients are factored into their multiples-of-p part and products over residues prime to p; pairing j with p^r-j and expanding these unit products reduces the required valuations to reciprocal power sums over the units, whose vanishing supplies the extra powers of p. An algebraic cancellation among the shifted products then combines these valuations with \binom{2p^L}{p^L}\equiv2 and \binom{3p^L}{p^L}\equiv3, using sharper separate exponents when p=3, to obtain the claimed modulus.
